reports.title: Relationship of menstrual history to altitude chamber decompression sickness.
reports.locator: Rudge pp. 657–658, Methods, Table I and Figure 1
reports.reason: Retain 81 selected DCS case records. Figure 1 gives 62 Type I and 19 Type II. The phase-specific exposed comparison group is unavailable. Preserve the table/figure daily-bin discrepancy and the overlap hold with the other USAF treatment archives.

reports.title: Occurrence of decompression sickness on descent from high altitudes.
reports.locator: Rodbard pp. 89–91, opening paragraph and Tables I–II
reports.reason: Retain selected routine training exposure case histories under existing identifiers. The 1944 bulletin and 1946 paper repeat numbered cases. Preserve six chokes and eight neurologic presentations in their source strata. No role-specific or overall exposure denominator.

reports.title: [Decompression sickness in hypobaric environment].
reports.locator: Ríos Tejada et al., Med Clin (Barc). 1998;111(9):359
reports.reason: Publication verified in NLM, the issue catalogue and the author's bibliography. Request the original page to identify the initiating setting and whether the earlier Spanish chamber report covers the same episode. DCS versus arterial gas embolism remains unresolved.

reports.title: [A twenty-seven year survey of hypobaric chamber physiological reactions of the Chinese Air Force].
reports.locator: Wen et al., Zhonghua Yi Xue Za Zhi (Taipei). 1988;41(2):103–108
reports.reason: Use the exact print holding for original tables. Keep Wen's February article distinct from Ho's December companion pending comparison. Fang's historical 696/15,370 is all-cause chamber reactions, and the later Taiwan cohort has separate dates. The accessible sources supply no matched clinical DCS numerator.

reports.title: Ten-year survey of altitude chamber reactions using the FAA training chamber flight profiles.
reports.locator: Valdez, p. 720 Table I and Results. FAA 1990 update Tables 1–2
reports.reason: Retain previously verified 0/3,034 Type A and 0/1,725 Type B student evolved-gas outcomes. Their aggregate of 4,759 is the same risk set, and two treated technician cases have a missing staff denominator. Later FAA surveillance nests the source dates. Retain the source endpoint and hold quantitative cohort selection.

reports.title: HYPOBARIC HYPOXIA TRAINING AND THE RELEVANCE OF DETERMINING THE SO-CALLED RESERVE TIME IN POLISH PILOTS – PRELIMINARY REPORT
reports.locator: Kopka et al., Defence medical institute historical statement, p. 29
reports.reason: The authors report zero DCS cases during the previous 20 years of WIML exposures. Exact dates, delayed ascertainment and a matching denominator remain unavailable. Use the previously registered report and keep the preliminary protocol sample separate.

observations.endpoint: author-reported DCS during the prior 20 years

reports.prior_assessment: Batch 03 assessed the same report under a supplementary occurrence. The review disposition is reaffirmed.

reports.title: Aviation Medicine
reports.reason: Signed review of the 1993 Harding and Mills textbook. No original chamber cohort or attributable cases.

reports.title: Hearing injuries due to atmospheric pressure changes in air and water survival training instructors
reports.locator: Methods and Results, PDF pp. 3–4; 2017 row of Table 2, PDF p. 5
reports.reason: Retain one author-defined 2017 decompression illness with hearing injury as a mixed-setting observation. Initiating activity and dates of symptom ascertainment are unavailable. The 20 instructors are an occupational population with air and water duties. Hold chamber case attribution and denominator eligibility.

observations.endpoint: reported decompression illness with hearing injury
